In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367)

title: Receipts/ReferencedGenericValueTypeTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (4/4), passes on head (4/4); refutes 2 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-1, requirement-tests-2

refutes.claim: The new helper `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` is documented as returning null for a metadata property, but it still indexes `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` unguarded. The `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` call site at line 985, which the reporter cited, therefore still throws `IndexOutOfRangeException` for a property of a referenced-assembly type. Wrapping `reportDiagnostic` with `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` does not help, because the location argument is evaluated before the wrapper runs. This misses the criterion that diagnostics needing a source location must not crash when the symbol has no declaring syntax.

The diff guards only two of the three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites the reporter named (old lines 735, 1009 and 1101). No hunk touches the site near line 735. If it is still indexed directly, the closed-generic metadata path can still crash. The new report filter cannot prevent this, because the exception occurs while building the diagnostic.
